name: code-morph
title: Code Morph
description: A code panel morphs between versions of a file: surviving tokens glide to their new line and column, removed code blurs out and new code fades in. The clip is 4.6 s long for the default two versions and 36-frame morph.
useWhen: A launch or product demo needs to show an API getting simpler, with before and after code in one panel and the surviving tokens visibly travelling to their new places.
A refactor, a new SDK call or a config change should read as one continuous edit instead of a hard cut between two screenshots.
A walkthrough builds one file up in two to four steps, each change landing on a highlighted line.
avoidWhen: The code should simply appear line by line, with no before and after: use a code block reveal.
The code should be typed out character by character: use a terminal or typewriter effect.
The camera should scan a long file while it reveals.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Filename
variables.description: Name shown on the editor tab.

variables.label: Code before
variables.description: First version of the file. Leave empty for the sample.

variables.label: Code after
variables.description: Version the panel morphs into. Leave empty for the sample.

variables.label: Morph at
variables.description: Frame the morph into the second version starts.

variables.label: Steps
variables.description: Optional JSON array of {at, code} versions (at = start frame at 30 fps). Overrides code before and after.

variables.label: Font size
variables.description: Code size in pixels at a 1280 x 720 frame; it scales with the frame.

variables.label: Highlight changes
variables.description: Hold a short accent highlight on the changed lines.

variables.label: Window dots
variables.description: Show the three window dots in the title bar.
